concept: A served agent writes the same store a direct call writes — and whether the Claude Code CLI can classify it is decided by the caller's message, not by the framework
triggers: does my served agent write memory correctly
claude code cannot categorise my memories
notCovered: the layout comparison against the CLI itself — sdk/claude-code-memory owns that, against a recorded session
recall quality: whether the right memory is found once stored
the React side and per-user stores

lessons.explains: The trip through theokit dev, HTTP and the agent changes nothing about the store's shape — the index entry and the file land in the same form a direct call produces
metadata.type is written only when the message declares a kind, so in a served app the browser or service composing the request decides whether the memory is classifiable
The declaration the framework's route gate reads, and what 'public' exposes once the agent remembers
A state-changing route is CSRF-protected by default, so a hand-built request is refused before it reaches the agent

evidence.claims: Starts a real theokit dev with no credential and drives two message forms through the same served agent: 'Remember (project): …' produces a memory carrying metadata.type, 'Remember: …' produces one carrying none. Both are stored — the difference is classification, not validity. Also asserts the index entry has the CLI's shape and that the boot refuses nothing.
